updates.name: Add a home internet gateway as line 2 with an eligible address, a promotion and an add-on
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to sign up a new customer for a phone and a home internet gateway in the same visit, so the customer leaves the store with service on their phone and internet at home.

Some background, because this is retail telecom and none of it is obvious. When a customer buys service in a Metro store, the rep creates an account and then adds a "line" to it for each device the customer is putting on that account. A phone is one line. Metro also sells home internet: instead of a phone, the customer takes home a small box (a "gateway") that picks up the Metro 5G signal and turns it into home Wi-Fi. Because it is fixed to the customer's home, the network has to check that 5G home internet actually reaches that street address before the sale can go ahead. That check is what the eligibility screen does.

Two rules shape this test. First, home internet is never the customer's first line — so this test opens a brand-new account, activates the phone as line 1, and only then adds the gateway as line 2. Second, once the address is approved and the acknowledgements are signed off, the gateway is sold exactly like a phone from that point on — it gets a phone number, a plan, and the rep can attach a promotion and an add-on service before taking payment. This test walks that whole sale, from the gateway's serial number through to the amount the rep is asked to collect.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2289 (screens and acceptance criteria), RTPL-2008 (Home internet epic)

## Preconditions
- Nothing pre-existing is needed — this test builds its own account from scratch. Home internet cannot be the first line on an account, so the phone is activated first as line 1 and the home internet gateway is added afterwards as line 2.
- The store is set up to sell home internet. If the home internet screens never appear for a gateway serial number, stop and contact the manual QA team before going further — the feature is switched off for the environment, not broken.

## Test data
- **New customer details:** Any test customer: a first name, a last name, a unique email address per run, and a street address with its zip code (for example 405 LEXINGTON AVE, 10174, NEW YORK, NY)  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — the Account information screen was read live and asks only for First name, Middle initial, Last name, Email, Address, Address 2, Zip code, City and State)_
- **Customer phone number for the identity check:** 2125551234  _(verified: QA / UAT3 — this number has passed the identity check in previous activation runs on this environment)_
- **Phone for line 1 (IMEI):** The next unused phone IMEI from the RTGO Data workbook  _(verified: RTGO Data workbook, UAT3 sheet — the workbook's Used column is unreliable, so take the first IMEI the app actually accepts. Which phone it is does not matter to this test)_
- **SIM card for line 1:** The next unused physical SIM card number from the RTGO Data workbook  _(verified: RTGO Data workbook, UAT3 sheet — same caveat; if a SIM is rejected, move to the next row)_
- **Home internet gateway IMEI (the gateway's serial number):** 999977129737997  _(verified: UAT3 2026-07-29 — this serial number was accepted as a home internet device and opened the home internet screens)_
- **Service address:** 31455 NORTHWESTERN HWY  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — rep screenshot of the acknowledgement screen reading "Good news - 5G home internet is available." for this address)_
- **City:** FARMINGTON  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — same screenshot, filled in automatically from the Zip Code)_
- **State:** MI  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — same screenshot, filled in automatically from the Zip Code)_
- **Zip Code:** 48334  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — same screenshot)_

## Automation Notes
- Stop at the payment screen. The gateway's serial number is only consumed when the payment is submitted, so ending here keeps the same test device reusable run after run.
- The plan, promotion and add-on offered for a home internet line are not fixed values — take whichever the environment offers. Nothing later in this test depends on which one is picked, only that it appears against the line and in the totals.
- If the gateway serial number is refused, or the home internet screens never appear, try the next candidate serial number from the RTGO Data workbook first. If none work, contact the manual QA team to get a working home internet gateway serial number — do not sit blocked and do not go hunting for data alone.
- CONFIRM BEFORE AUTOMATING: the exact wording on the SIM step for a home internet line was not re-checked live on 2026-09-04 (the environment could not be reached). Record what the screen actually says on the first run and correct this ticket.
- The account and the phone line are built by this test, not assumed. If the phone IMEI or the SIM is rejected, take the next row from the RTGO Data workbook; if the whole pool is exhausted, contact the manual QA team for working device data rather than sitting blocked.
- CONFIRM BEFORE AUTOMATING: the account screens were re-read live on 2026-09-04 only as far as "Account information" — the environment refused to create the account past that point that day. Confirm the identity-check screen and the phone-line steps on the first run and correct this ticket if the app asks for anything else.

updates.name: Refuse an incomplete or invalid home internet service address before the eligibility check
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want the home internet address screen to stop me before I send an incomplete or nonsense address for checking, so the customer is never told their home is covered on the strength of a bad address.

Some background. Metro sells home internet as a small box (a "gateway") that the customer takes home and that turns the Metro 5G signal into home Wi-Fi. Because the box only works at one place, the network checks the customer's street address before the sale can go ahead. Everything downstream — whether the sale is allowed at all, and the paperwork the customer signs promising to use the box only at that address — hangs off the address the rep types on this one screen. So the screen has to hold the line on its own: an address that is empty, too short, too long, or a Zip Code that is not five digits must never reach the eligibility check.

This test pushes bad values at that form on purpose and confirms the rep is kept on the screen with a plain message each time, then confirms the form does accept a proper address and fills in the city and state from the Zip Code by itself.

This test starts from nothing: it opens a new account and activates a phone as line 1 first, because home internet can never be a customer's first line, and only then puts the gateway on as line 2.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2289 (screens and acceptance criteria), RTPL-2008 (Home internet epic)

## Preconditions
- Nothing pre-existing is needed — this test builds its own account from scratch. Home internet cannot be the first line on an account, so the phone is activated first as line 1 and the home internet gateway is added afterwards as line 2.
- The store is set up to sell home internet. If the home internet screens never appear for a gateway serial number, stop and contact the manual QA team before going further — the feature is switched off for the environment, not broken.

## Test data
- **New customer details:** Any test customer: a first name, a last name, a unique email address per run, and a street address with its zip code (for example 405 LEXINGTON AVE, 10174, NEW YORK, NY)  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — the Account information screen was read live and asks only for First name, Middle initial, Last name, Email, Address, Address 2, Zip code, City and State)_
- **Customer phone number for the identity check:** 2125551234  _(verified: QA / UAT3 — this number has passed the identity check in previous activation runs on this environment)_
- **Phone for line 1 (IMEI):** The next unused phone IMEI from the RTGO Data workbook  _(verified: RTGO Data workbook, UAT3 sheet — the workbook's Used column is unreliable, so take the first IMEI the app actually accepts. Which phone it is does not matter to this test)_
- **SIM card for line 1:** The next unused physical SIM card number from the RTGO Data workbook  _(verified: RTGO Data workbook, UAT3 sheet — same caveat; if a SIM is rejected, move to the next row)_
- **Home internet gateway IMEI (the gateway's serial number):** 999977129737997  _(verified: UAT3 2026-07-29 — this serial number was accepted as a home internet device and opened the home internet screens)_
- **Too-short address:** A  _(verified: Shipped build 2026-09-04 — the Address field on this screen requires at least 2 characters)_
- **Too-long address:** 31455 NORTHWESTERN HIGHWAY SUITE 100  _(verified: Shipped build 2026-09-04 — 36 characters, over the 30-character limit the Address field on this screen allows)_
- **Letters typed into Zip Code:** ABCDE  _(verified: Shipped build 2026-09-04 — the Zip Code field on this screen takes 5 digits only)_
- **Incomplete Zip Code:** 483  _(verified: Shipped build 2026-09-04 — city and state are only filled in once all 5 digits are entered)_
- **Valid Zip Code:** 48334  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — rep screenshot showing this Zip Code filling City as FARMINGTON and State as MI)_

## Automation Notes
- This test never sends an address for checking — it only proves the screen refuses bad input. It deliberately stops one click short of the eligibility check.
- The wording of each message is fixed by the app and is worth asserting exactly, because a reworded or missing message is what lets a bad address through unnoticed.
- If the gateway serial number is refused, or the home internet screens never appear, try the next candidate serial number from the RTGO Data workbook first. If none work, contact the manual QA team to get a working home internet gateway serial number — do not sit blocked and do not go hunting for data alone.
- CONFIRM BEFORE AUTOMATING: on the too-long address, record which of the two behaviours the build actually shows — the field capping at 30 characters, or the "Address cannot exceed 30 characters" message — and narrow this step to the one you see. The environment could not be reached on 2026-09-04 to settle it.
- The account and the phone line are built by this test, not assumed. If the phone IMEI or the SIM is rejected, take the next row from the RTGO Data workbook; if the whole pool is exhausted, contact the manual QA team for working device data rather than sitting blocked.
- CONFIRM BEFORE AUTOMATING: the account screens were re-read live on 2026-09-04 only as far as "Account information" — the environment refused to create the account past that point that day. Confirm the identity-check screen and the phone-line steps on the first run and correct this ticket if the app asks for anything else.

updates.name: Back out of the home internet screens and land back on IMEI validation
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want Back on either home internet screen to put me back at the point where I enter the device's serial number, so that when a customer changes their mind I can start the line over cleanly instead of being stranded mid-sale.

Some background. Metro sells home internet as a small box (a "gateway") the customer takes home, which turns the Metro 5G signal into home Wi-Fi. Because the box only works at one address, selling one puts the rep through two extra screens a phone sale never sees: a screen where the customer's street address is checked for coverage, and a screen where both the customer and the rep have to sign off that the box will only be used at that address. A rep in a store backs out of these all the time — the customer is not sure of the address, or decides against home internet once they hear the terms.

What has to happen in that case is specific: Back must take the rep all the way back to the serial-number screen, NOT one step back to the address form, and it must leave nothing behind. The line being built is dropped, the same gateway can be entered again straight away, and the address form comes up blank rather than holding the last address that was typed. This test does it from both screens in turn and checks where the rep lands each time.

This test starts from nothing: it opens a new account and activates a phone as line 1 first, because home internet can never be a customer's first line, and only then starts the gateway on line 2.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2289 AC-9 (Back from the acknowledgement returns to device validation), RTPL-2008 (Home internet epic)

## Preconditions
- Nothing pre-existing is needed — this test builds its own account from scratch. Home internet cannot be the first line on an account, so the phone is activated first as line 1 and the home internet gateway is added afterwards as line 2.
- The store is set up to sell home internet. If the home internet screens never appear for a gateway serial number, stop and contact the manual QA team before going further — the feature is switched off for the environment, not broken.

- **New customer details:** Any test customer: a first name, a last name, a unique email address per run, and a street address with its zip code (for example 405 LEXINGTON AVE, 10174, NEW YORK, NY)  _(verified: QA / UAT3 2026-09-04 — the Account information screen was read live and asks only for First name, Middle initial, Last name, Email, Address, Address 2, Zip code, City and State)_

- **SIM card for line 1:** The next unused physical SIM card number from the RTGO Data workbook  _(verified: RTGO Data workbook, UAT3 sheet — same caveat; if a SIM is rejected, move to the next row)_

- The point of this test is WHERE the rep lands. Landing on the address form instead of the serial-number screen is the failure this test exists to catch — it is called out explicitly in the requirement for this screen.
